title: Notes on first-order optimization
section: 1.2 Step size and convergence on a quadratic
focus: Explain gradient descent on the one-dimensional quadratic f(x) = (a/2) x^2. Let the learner change the curvature a, the step size eta, the starting point and the number of steps. Show the sequence of iterates and of f values. Check that 0 < eta < 2/a converges, eta = 1/a reaches the minimum in one step, and eta > 2/a diverges.

Gradient descent minimizes a differentiable function f by repeatedly stepping against its gradient: x_(k+1) = x_k - eta * f'(x_k), where eta > 0 is the step size. For the quadratic f(x) = (a/2) x^2 with a > 0 the update becomes x_(k+1) = (1 - eta * a) x_k, so the iterates shrink towards the minimum at 0 exactly when |1 - eta * a| < 1, that is when 0 < eta < 2 / a. For eta = 1 / a the minimum is reached in a single step; for 1/a < eta < 2/a the iterates overshoot and alternate in sign while still converging; for eta > 2/a they diverge.
